items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: Steeplehead Johnson. He was the piano player.... Freddy Johnson. He had just come back from Europe; he was the piano player.

ctx.x: So from that point on, and while I'm working up there a few weeks, a fellow offered me a job with Billy Fowler's band at the Club Alabam on Broadway. This was a big-time nightclub down on 44th Street, big show, chorus, showgirls, comedians, a great big band was down there -- Jimmy Wade's band was working in there at the present, and Billy was going to take his place. So I reported for rehearsal down there. And boy, I've never seen nothing so beautiful in all my life. The club was beautiful. All the chorus girls…

And here's the band now; here's Billy Fowler. I don't know any of them, you know. I don't know Billy. Billy was a helluva nice guy. He had heard about me, and he was glad that I could join the band. Edgar Sampson was in the band. Steeplehead Johnson. He was the piano player.... Freddy Johnson. He had just come back from Europe; he was the piano player. No, he hadn't went to Europe. He was the piano player. A fellow named Ward Pinkett, the trumpet player. Cuffee...
